title: Partner intro: Redwood <> Halcyon Systems - partner discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Halcyon Systems. Halcyon is a GPU cloud provider focused on enterprise edge and regulated customers; exploring partnership for offering Redwood Dedicated/Private on Halcyon's infra and potential reseller/integration opportunities. Key topics: current infra (k8s + H100 bare metal), data residency and SOC2/ISO concerns, pilot scope (6-8 week proof-of-concept), latency vs cost tradeoffs, and next steps to share security docs, run benchmarks, and align partnership commercial model.
topics: Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
action_items: Samir Patel: Send partner one-pager + Redwood partner deck by 2026-03-30
Jordan Li: Share initial benchmark plan and request for Halcyon's test cluster access by 2026-03-31
Aisha Gomez: Intro Halcyon to Redwood partnerships lead (formal intro email) - due 2026-03-29
Maya Chen: Provide inventory of current GPU types, average concurrency, and sample customer SLAs by 2026-04-02
next_steps: Schedule technical deep dive / benchmark session (SE-led) w/ Halcyon infra team
Share SOC2, ISO27001, and security architecture docs
Define pilot scope and acceptance criteria (latency, throughput, cost targets)
Align on commercial model (reseller vs referral vs joint offering)
Set up access for Redwood SE to run latency and throughput tests on Halcyon test cluster
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-27 15:00 PDT | Duration: 38m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Aisha Gomez (Redwood Partnerships), Maya Chen (Halcyon Head of Platform), Luis Ortega (CTO), Priya Nair (Infra), Evan Brooks (Security)

[00:00] Samir Patel (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Samir, account lead for Redwood. With me is Jordan, our SE, and Aisha from partnerships. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya Chen (Halcyon): Hi Samir, doing well, thanks. I'm Maya. Luis and Priya on our side, plus Evan for security.
[00:12] Luis Ortega (Halcyon): Morning all, quick note we may have spotty audio, apologies in advance.
[00:18] Samir Patel: No worries. Quick agenda: quick intros, learn about Halcyon's infra and partner goals, discuss integration possibilities ( Dedicated, Private), security and compliance needs, then define pilot and next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Maya: Yep, sounds great. I'll kick off with a quick Halcyon overview. We're a GPU cloud provider focused on enterprise edge and regulated verticals, we sell both capacity and managed clusters. We run a mixture of bare-metal H100s and A100s across our regions. Our customers care about data residency and on-prem-like isolation.
[00:45] Priya Nair (Halcyon): From infra we run Kubernetes in a thin control plane and a dedicated provisioning layer for bare metal nodes. We have some customers on air-gapped installs as well.
[00:56] Jordan Li (Redwood): Okay that's helpful. Are you seeing a lot of inference workloads already or is this a channel/partnership motion?
[01:02] Maya: It's both. Some customers ask for turnkey inference stacks. We're exploring partnering with inference platform vendors to provide a managed experience and also possibly resell.
[01:12] Aisha Gomez (Redwood): Great, that's exactly the sort of partner motion we do — give customers Redwood's runtime plus your infra.
[01:18] Evan Brooks (Halcyon): Quick security preface: we need SOC2 and ISO artifacts, tight KMS controls, and SSO/SAML. For on-prem customers we oft have specific audit requirements.
[01:28] Samir: Understood. Redwood has SOC2, ISO 27001 — we'll share docs. We offer KMS integration and support customer-managed keys in private deployments.
[01:36] Luis: Cool. On technical constraints: latency and cost are the big levers. Some of our customers want sub-150ms response for short chat-ish queries at tail p99, others tolerate higher. How does Redwood think about latency/cost trade-offs?
[01:51] Jordan: We typically recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput and low-latency SLOs; Private for customers who require full network isolation and KMS control. We can do batching and KV prefix caching to reduce cost while preserving p50 latency; tail p99 depends on load shaping and instance types.
[02:10] Priya: Do you support mixed GPU types, e.g., H100 and L40s? Our fleet mixes vendors.
[02:16] Jordan: Yes, Redwood runtime supports heterogenous hardware; we can route by policy to appropriate variants. We do selection of quantized kernels per device. Worth noting quantization options may change quality and perf.
[02:28] Maya: Any experience with NVidia H100 bare metal? We sometimes see driver quirks with inference runtimes.
[02:34] Jordan: We run H100 a lot in our benchmarks; kernel selection and compilation stage matter. We can provide performance profiles we've validated on H100. We'll share our benchmark spreadsheet.
[02:46] Samir: On the partnership level, we usually have a few motions: 1) reseller/managed offering where Halcyon sells Redwood-powered endpoints; 2) integration where joint customers use Halcyon infra with Redwood Private; or 3) referral with revenue share. Which sounds right?
[03:02] Maya: I think we want a flexible approach. Early on we might do referral + technical integration, then move to reseller for enterprise deals.
[03:12] Evan: Security question: for Private deployments, where do audit logs live? Can they be shipped to our SIEM?
[03:19] Jordan: Yes, we can forward audit logs to customer-managed SIEMs and provide API/webhook hooks. Logs can be stored locally or forwarded. We'll include log retention options in docs.
[03:29] Luis: What about model provenance and customer data retention? Some of our customers are fin/health and require no cross-tenant caching.
[03:36] Samir: We support tenant isolation and can disable cross-tenant caching. For Hosted we do multi-tenancy by default but Enterprises can use Dedicated/Private. We'll share the model and data handling whitepaper.
[03:46] Maya: Great. On ops side, what's the onboarding like? We generally want a small pilot cluster and then staged rollouts.
[03:54] Jordan: Typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: initial config, run benchmarks, validate SLOs, then expand. We'll need access to a test cluster (or we can provision on our side). For tests we measure token throughput, latency p50/p95/p99, and cost per 1k tokens for representative prompts.
[04:12] Priya: We prefer Redwood to run tests on our infra to capture realistic perf. Is that possible?
[04:17] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll request limited access and credentials; we'd use an ephemeral test harness and share methodology. We'll limit scope and wipe artifacts after testing.
[04:27] Aisha: From partnerships we can discuss go-to-market materials and joint marketing once we have a pilot success.
[04:33] Maya: Sounds good. Pricing — do you have partner pricing or referral discounts?
[04:38] Samir: We have partner tiers; early partners typically get referral credits and preferred renewal rates. Aisha will follow up on specifics.
[04:45] Evan: A few technical nitty-gritty: network topology for Private — can Redwood run in VPC on our cloud or in our bare-metal customer environments?
[04:54] Jordan: Yes, Private supports VPC deployments and on-prem packaging. For air-gapped installs we have a deployment bundle and an offline installer; we work with infra teams to validate. There can be operational overhead for on-prem but we have an integration playbook.
[05:10] Luis: How do you handle model updates and rollouts? We need control over versions per customer.
[05:15] Jordan: We support pinning model versions per deployment and have rollout primitives (canary, A/B, automatic fallback). Model artifacts are stored in customer-controlled buckets for Private.
[05:25] Maya: Any limitations on supported models? We mainly see Llama/Starling-type open models from customers plus some proprietary.
[05:31] Jordan: We support a wide catalog; our model onboarding team can work to validate a given model. For proprietary models we can work with customer-provided artifacts subject to licensing.
[05:42] Samir: Let's dig into pilot success criteria. Maya, what's an acceptable latency and throughput target for your early customers?
[05:48] Maya: For chat use-case, p50 below 80ms, p95 below 200ms is ideal but p99 can be higher. Throughput wise, we want to be able to sustain 300 concurrent small-reqs for a single tenant. Those are rough numbers.
[06:00] Jordan: Those are reasonable targets. We'll capture baseline on H100 nodes and advise on instance sizing. Caching can help at tail for repeated prompts.
[06:10] Priya: Regarding KV cache — do you support prefix caching across requests? Some of our tenants reuse prompts heavily.
[06:16] Jordan: Yes, prefix and KV caching are part of the runtime; we can configure TTLs and isolation. For regulated customers we can disable or ensure per-tenant-only caches.
[06:26] Luis: On the billing/reconciliation side, how granular are usage reports?
[06:31] Samir: We provide token-level reporting, per-route cost breakdowns, and per-token latency. We can export to your billing pipelines or provide CSVs/APIs.
[06:41] Evan: Encryption at rest and in transit — we require customer-managed KMS and TLS to internal networks.
[06:47] Jordan: Supported. For Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we can support customer-managed keys as well.
[06:55] Maya: Any known gotchas running Redwood on mixed-hardware fleets?
[07:00] Jordan: The main thing is kernel selection and quantization variants. You'll want consistent driver versions; we'll share recommended driver matrix. Also batch size and concurrency tuning per model family matter.
[07:10] Samir: For the benchmark, Jordan will propose a test plan. Aisha will coordinate the partnership terms. We'll also share a short partner one-pager and security artifacts.
[07:20] Maya: Cool. A quick question — we have a few strategic customers already using ApexCloud and VertexCloud solutions. How do you compare on control and cost?
[07:29] Samir: We position Redwood as production-first: strong latency and cost levers (batching, caching, quantization) plus consistent operations across hosted/dedicated/private. In many cases customers see lower unit cost at scale compared to managed endpoints because of caching and better runtime efficiency. We'll send comparative notes (high level).
[07:43] Evan: On audit trails — can you provide immutable logs for 7 years? Some of our customers demand long retention.
[07:50] Jordan: Log retention is configurable; for Private deployments it would be under customer control, so yes, we can meet long retention via your storage. Hosted has limits but can be extended via add-on. We'll include options.
[08:02] Luis: Let's lock on timeline: if we start the pilot next week, 6-8 weeks to pilot completion and then GTM. Is that realistic?
[08:10] Samir: Yes, realistic. We'll need the cluster details and a signed NDA if needed for deeper access.
[08:16] Maya: NDA is fine. We'll prepare an environment snapshot and credentials for a test tenant.
[08:22] Jordan: For the benchmark plan we'll request sample prompts, payload sizes, concurrency profiles, and a small corpus for evals.
[08:30] Priya: We'll share that — also our current orchestration uses a custom operator on top of k8s; will that be compatible?
[08:36] Jordan: Likely yes; our SEs have integrated with custom provisioning layers before. We'll validate during the technical deep dive.
[08:44] Samir: Any other blockers from your side?
[08:47] Maya: Nothing major. Security wants to review SOC2 and architecture, but that's standard.
[08:52] Evan: We'll want a runbook for incident response and support SLAs.
[08:56] Samir: We can provide an enterprise SLA doc and runbook examples.
[09:00] Maya: Okay good. Quick commercial: are you open to a co-selling arrangement for some accounts?
[09:05] Aisha: Yes, we have partner programs for co-sell and reseller motions; specifics depend on volume commitments. We'll scope that after pilot.
[09:14] Luis: One more technical — what monitoring/tracing hooks do you expose? We need per-route tracing and per-token latency metrics to feed into our observability.
[09:23] Jordan: We expose per-request trace IDs, metrics, and token-level timings, plus integrations for OpenTelemetry and common APMs. We'll include sample dashboards.
[09:33] Maya: Perfect.
[09:35] Samir: Wrap-up time — recap: Redwood to send partner deck, security artifacts, preliminary benchmark plan; Halcyon to share infra inventory, concurrency profiles, and provide test cluster access; schedule SE-led benchmark session next week. Anything to add?
[09:50] Priya: We'll try to have a small test cluster ready within a week.
[09:54] Evan: We'll review security docs and get back with any follow-ups.
[09:58] Aisha: I'll coordinate the intro to our partnerships head and send next steps.
[10:02] Samir: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
[10:06] Maya: Thanks all.

[End of transcript]

Notes: Transcript includes occasional minor transcription errors and generic speaker labels in places due to the auto-transcription. References: Samir to send Redwood partner deck (link placeholder), Jordan to share benchmark spreadsheet (link placeholder).
